newsitem.title: UK: Cable & Wireless dips on Sprint talk.
newsitem.headline: Cable & Wireless dips on Sprint talk.

text.p: Shares in Cable & Wireless Plc were down 1p to 505 by 0835 GMT, following press reports that the company is considering making a bid for U.S. telecoms group Sprint Corp.

The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that the British telecommunications company was talking with France Telecom FTE.PA. and Germany's Deutsche Telekom, each of whom own ten percent of Sprint shares.
"A bid by C&W would make sense. If they are going to compete in a global market they have to find a partner," the head of trading at a large brokerage said.
A link-up between Cable & Wireless and Sprint would create the world's 15th largest telecommunications group, in terms of market capitalisation, according to Reuters Securities 3000.
Sprint's current market capitalisation is around $14.5 billion while C&W is valued at $11.3 billion. No one at Cable & Wireless was immediately available to comment.

Concert, a proposed merger of British Telecommunications U.S. group MCI Corp would, if approved, create the world's second largest telecommunications company, with the combined company capitalised at $66.89 billion.
